title: Playing with Dink Johnson and gigs out west
summary: Allen asks about Dink Johnson; Hall played a few one-nighters with him and says most of his California work was with Mutt Carey and Ory.

story.theme_name: Going west: California and the Los Angeles scene
story.community_name: Going west: moving to and working in California

blocks.x: At that time, that very first one, 1921, Dink Johnson played clarinetti. That's right, yeah. He played little drums. He'd been with Freddie Keppard and his brother Bill. Did you ever play with Dink? A few, like little one nights, you know. When he played piano then, I guess?
Yeah, yeah. Because I played once with him at Son of Barber. He lived up there.
He lived up there. I knew Dink very well when he had a place up by the ballpark, you know. That's right. Yeah, by the ballpark.

I made some records with him. Yeah, yeah. But I just, just gigs we called. Yeah. No, I never played. All the work, most I played out here with, was between Mutt and Ory. Well, practically Ory. At the time, I was working with this band in the war with Winslow Allen. Over the place they call it Strip City now. Peacorn Western. We were working at nightclub. That's why I got drafted in Army again.
